name: Guardian cryptic crossword, Penguin book 2 No 3

book.title: The New Penguin Book of The Guardian Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Imposing old lady, an active person, about to wiggle

indicators.note: one word goes about another, wrapping round it on both sides

blocks.note: someone active is a doer
to wag is to wiggle, as a dog's tail does

explanation.surface: A formidable elderly lady, still busy, is about to start dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: About looks like part of 'about to', meaning on the point of, but it is the wrapping signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title from her late husband, typically a grand and formidable elderly woman.

clue.text: Lobster, possibly, a party deliberately walked over

indicators.note: turned over in a down entry, the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: a do is a party
to pace is to walk with measured steps

explanation.surface: Someone carefully strides across a crustacean at a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Decapods are ten-legged crustaceans, and the lobster is one example, hence possibly.

clue.text: A carnivore cannot but feel pain having eaten nothing — it droops

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater

blocks.note: the walrus is a meat-eating sea mammal
if one cannot do otherwise, one must
to hurt dully
zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A meat-eater, in pain from an empty stomach, wilts.
explanation.walkthrough: The nought sits just after the first letter of the second word. The style is named for the walrus's own drooping whiskers.
explanation.definitionFit: A walrus moustache is a thick, long moustache hanging down over the mouth like the animal's whiskers.

clue.text: A diagram I consider practically vivid

indicators.note: practically means nearly, so the word is not quite complete and its last letter goes

blocks.note: a graph is a diagram of data
taken as written
to call is to consider, as in call it a day; last letter dropped

explanation.surface: Someone finds a chart pretty striking.
explanation.walkthrough: Call means consider, as in I call that rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphic or graphical description is clear and lifelike, so the word also means vivid.

clue.text: Aegean island's sound tracks

indicators.note: only the spoken sound of the island's name matters

blocks.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean

explanation.surface: A Greek island has well-made paths.
explanation.walkthrough: Sound reads as an adjective, healthy, but it signals what the name sounds like.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracks are paths or ways for travel, the same general idea as roads.

clue.text: Holy man, eastern, appearing in haze to swagger

indicators.note: the holy man and the compass point show up inside the word for haze

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
E is the abbreviation for east or eastern
a haze makes things a blur

explanation.surface: An eastern holy man looms out of the mist, strutting.
explanation.definitionFit: To bluster is to talk or behave in a loud, boastful, aggressive way, much like swaggering.

clue.text: Instructions must be concise in the General Staff

blocks.note: short and to the point
taken as written
GS is the military abbreviation for General Staff

explanation.surface: Army orders issued by senior staff officers should be kept short.
explanation.walkthrough: In looks like a container signal but is simply part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefings are sets of information and orders given before an operation, which are instructions.

clue.text: A sleeping place in Paris left in darkness?

blocks.note: un is French for a
lit is French for bed

explanation.surface: A Paris hotel bed is left without a light on.
explanation.walkthrough: In Paris applies to both words, which are read as French.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means having no light, so a place left unlit stays dark; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Was careful beforehand to stick one oar up with a swing

indicators.note: a swing throws everything about, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A rower carefully raises one oar while swinging round.
explanation.definitionFit: To take precautions is to act in advance to guard against risk, being careful ahead of time.

clue.text: Geographical areas offering free mixed gins

indicators.note: mixed drinks are blended, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: to rid is to free of something
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some regions hand out complimentary cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire was historically divided into three ridings, North, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: A riding is an old administrative division of a county, notably Yorkshire, so a territorial district.

clue.text: I'd call MO man's pal, in a way, superficially unruffled

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged in some way, set out in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these words, apostrophes dropped

explanation.surface: Someone muses on naming a friend of a medical officer's, apparently unflustered.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill pond is dammed water with a glassy surface, so the phrase describes outward calm with no visible ripples.

clue.text: The start of profligacy? Oh, that hurts the pocket

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: first letter
the cry of pain

explanation.surface: Spending freely begins with a wince, as one's wallet takes the hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pocket sounds like money, but a pouch is a small bag or pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A pouch is a small bag, and in clothing a pocket is exactly such a sewn-in bag.

clue.text: Emergency clasp? Yes, if pants mostly torn!

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped
something torn is ripped apart, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: A wardrobe malfunction: if your trousers are ripped, a quick fastener saves the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety pin is the standard improvised fastener grabbed when clothing tears, hence a clasp for emergencies.

clue.text: Mother has nothing free from dirt, threatening imminent danger

blocks.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
zero, shaped like O
without dirt

explanation.surface: A mother has nothing clean, a domestic crisis looming.
explanation.walkthrough: Damocles sat beneath a sword hung by a single hair, so Damoclean means precariously threatened.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from the legend of the sword of Damocles, a peril hanging over someone at any moment.

clue.text: Absolve former copper beginning to lose head

indicators.note: only the beginning, the first letter, of the next word is used

blocks.note: ex- means former
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
first letter
the pate is the top of the head

explanation.surface: An ex-policeman is cleared just as he starts to lose his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer but is the metal, Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: To exculpate is to clear someone of blame, which is what absolving them does.

clue.text: Ships' companies sailing to and fro, we hear

indicators.note: the word is identified by how it is heard spoken, not how it is written

blocks.note: a cruise is a voyage sailing about for pleasure

explanation.surface: Sailors are seen heading back and forth, or so we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's company is the whole body of people working aboard, which is its crew.

clue.text: Thwart the head, and anger results

blocks.note: to cross someone is to thwart them
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Frustrating your boss leads to fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The head is a promontory of land, not a boss, as in place names like Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossness is bad temper or annoyance, a mild form of anger.

clue.text: A capital case

blocks.note: surface reading: a court case punishable by death, or an upper-case letter
setter's reading: the bony case that holds the head, capital being from Latin caput

explanation.walkthrough: Capital suggests a death-penalty trial or a big letter; here it means of the head, and case means container.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony structure enclosing the brain is literally a case for the head.

clue.text: What's afoot on board ship? English sailor's covered in smut

indicators.note: the covering word surrounds the others like a coating

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
an AB is an able seaman
smut is a flake of soot

explanation.surface: What is going on aboard? An English sailor is filthy with grime.
explanation.walkthrough: Afoot means happening, but here it means worn on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea boot is a high waterproof boot worn by sailors, literally what is on a foot aboard ship.

clue.text: Flightless bird, almost completely shy, and so cautious

indicators.note: nearly all of the word is kept, its last letter lost

blocks.note: to shy is to throw or cast; without its last letter
taken as written
being on guard

explanation.surface: A bird that cannot fly is timid and therefore careful.
explanation.walkthrough: Shy reads as timid, but it is the verb to throw, as at a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: The cassowary is a large ostrich-like bird of New Guinea and Australia that cannot fly.

clue.text: Pay finally deserved and greatly desired

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

blocks.note: last letter
merited by effort

explanation.surface: A long-awaited wage, at last earned and much wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for intensely, so yearned means wanted very much.

clue.text: RA curtail comic — it's near the knuckle, perhaps?

indicators.note: a comic treatment plays about with them, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: An academician is told to cut a risqué comedian's act short.
explanation.walkthrough: Near the knuckle usually means risqué; here it means literally near a joint. RA is a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: Articular means relating to the joints, and the knuckle is a finger joint, so the example fits.

clue.text: Youngster rebuked around start of lesson

indicators.note: just the first letter of the following word is taken
one word goes around the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: chid is an old past tense of chide
first letter

explanation.surface: A pupil is told off as the class begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A child is a young person, and youngster is an everyday word for one.

clue.text: Directed — in a straight line?

blocks.note: first meaning: governed or controlled
second meaning: marked with straight lines drawn by a ruler

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one idea, directed straight, but splits into governing and lines drawn with a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule is to govern, and ruled paper bears straight lines drawn with a ruler.

clue.text: Buddhist literature and paintings, etc., American brought back

indicators.note: the combined letters are brought back, read from right to left

blocks.note: painting and the like are art
US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Buddhist texts and artworks are repatriated by an American.
explanation.definitionFit: A sutra is a scripture or aphorism in Buddhist and Hindu writing, a sermon of the Buddha.

clue.text: As soon as elected, a college sportsman has daydream very rarely

blocks.note: once, as in once he arrives
a winning candidate is in
taken as written
a Blue has represented Oxford or Cambridge at a sport
to moon about is to daydream

explanation.surface: A university athlete, just picked, drifts into reverie.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is someone who has played for Oxford or Cambridge University against the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue moon, a second full moon in one month, is uncommon, so the idiom means hardly ever.

clue.text: In the street, read letters and pedal

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: running across the end of street, read and the start of letters

explanation.surface: Someone stands on the street reading their post, then cycles off.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated lever driving a machine such as a sewing machine or lathe, a kind of pedal.

clue.text: Princess's various dues no longer in force

indicators.note: various suggests varied forms, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: Di is Princess Diana, with the possessive s
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal's assorted fees are no longer being charged.
explanation.walkthrough: Di was the popular name of Diana, Princess of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disused has fallen out of use, as a law or rule no longer in force has.
